new_page.title: How to Appeal Your BC Assessment: Deadline & Steps
new_page.h1: How do I appeal my BC Assessment?
new_page.description: Call BC Assessment first. If you still disagree, file a complaint with the Property Assessment Review Panel by January 31. What evidence helps.

breadcrumbs.name: How do I appeal my BC Assessment?

faq.q: Is my BC Assessment what my home would sell for?
faq.a: Not exactly. It reflects the market on July 1 of the year before, and a mass appraisal can miss your home's details. For a current price, ask for a market evaluation.

faq.q: Does it cost money to appeal?
faq.a: Filing with the Property Assessment Review Panel has no fee listed by BC Assessment. A further appeal to the Property Assessment Appeal Board has a fee.

parts.t: Call BC Assessment first: many values are fixed by agreement without a hearing. If you still disagree, file a complaint with the Property Assessment Review Panel by January 31 of the assessment year (the date can move when it falls on a weekend). The panel hears complaints from February to March.

items.t: Check the property details on your notice: lot size, floor area, bedrooms, suites, age
Compare with sales of similar homes near the valuation date
Call BC Assessment and ask for a review
If that does not settle it, file a Notice of Complaint by the January deadline
Bring your evidence to the panel hearing; you can appeal further to the Property Assessment Appeal Board

parts.t: Sales of truly similar homes close to the valuation date, and facts the assessor got wrong (an unpermitted suite counted as legal, the wrong lot size, a home that needs major repairs). A higher or lower tax bill is not a reason the panel can use.
Property tax is shared out by value, so your bill drops only if your value falls relative to the rest of your area. A correction still matters for the home owner grant if you are near the threshold.
Read on November 18, 2026. Rules change, so confirm with the source or your lawyer, notary or accountant before you act.
